text: Git branching helps developers work on different tasks without affecting the main code. In a typical version control workflow, you create a feature branch to add a new feature or fix a bug. This keeps your changes separate from the stable main branch. When your work is ready, you merge the feature branch back into the main branch. Before merging, many teams use pull requests so others can review the code and suggest improvements. This process makes teamwork easier and safer, because mistakes can be fixed before they reach the main project. Learning branching is an important step for anyone working with Git.
